title: Kähler differentials commute with localization of the algebra
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings, $S\subset B$ a multiplicative subset and $S^{-1}B$ the localization, an $A$-algebra via $A\to B\to S^{-1}B$. Then the $S^{-1}B$-linear map $S^{-1}\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{S^{-1}B/A}$, $\mathrm db/s\mapsto(1/s)\,\mathrm d(b/1)$, induced by the map $\Omega_{B/A}\to\Omega_{S^{-1}B/A}$ of $B\to S^{-1}B$ ($\Omega$ and $\mathrm d$ as in [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]), is an isomorphism. In particular, for $g\in B$, $\Omega_{B_g/A}\cong(\Omega_{B/A})_g$.
